Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Porter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Jill Aaron (CTO, Horizon Health), Marcus Lee (Head of MLOps), Sofia Ramos (Security), Danny Vu (ML Engineer)
Recording: yes
Links: deck (shared), benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared), SOC2 snapshot (will be sent)
summary: Discovery / scoping call to align on POC goals for Horizon Health's clinical document understanding use case. Discussed workload sizing, latency/throughput targets, data residency and security constraints, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing & security docs; customer to share workload samples and success criteria; schedule benchmark window mid-March.
transcript:
[00:00:05] Ethan Porter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're excited to chat through the POC scoping for the clinical NLP work you mentioned. Um quick intros?
[00:00:15] Jill Aaron: Hi, Jill here, CTO at Horizon Health, I'll be owning the outcome, thanks for setting this up.
[00:00:22] Marcus Lee: Marcus, Head of MLOps, I'll be the technical point for the tests and infra questions.
[00:00:27] Sofia Ramos: Sofia, security and compliance, I'll be asking about SOC2, KMS and network isolation.
[00:00:33] Ethan Porter: Awesome, and Maya, do you want to intro?
[00:00:36] Maya Singh: Sure, Maya Singh, Redwood Solutions Engineer. I run the benchmark and pilot setups, we'll try to scope the workload so we can give a tight recommendation on hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:00:45] Danny Vu: Danny, ML engineer, I'll be running the tests and looking at quality metrics.
[00:01:02] Ethan Porter: Great. High level, can you walk us through the current workflow you want to POC? Marcus?
[00:01:10] Marcus Lee: Yeah so we're ingesting clinical notes, about 20k new notes a day, but primary POC is a batch/near-RT extraction pipeline. Typical request size is between 200-800 tokens, tokens per doc varies. We'll run maybe 200 requests per second at peak for short periods, average probably 40-60 rps across business hours. Latency target we'd like is p95 < 300ms for inference, ideally < 200ms but we know that's aggressive. Accuracy: we need equal-or-better F1 vs our current model, and no regressions on key entity classes.
[00:01:55] Maya Singh: Okay, that gives us good starting numbers. Two clarifying q's: how sensitive is the data (PHI), and do you need data to never leave your VPC?
[00:02:05] Sofia Ramos: Yes PHI, patient data. We have strict policies - we prefer private or dedicated with VPC peering. Hosted might be acceptable if we can confirm customer-managed encryption keys and strong contractual controls, plus data residency in the region.
[00:02:22] Ethan Porter: Understood. So the main decision axes are: cost/ops effort, latency at peak, and security/data residency. We'll walk through tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and the smallest ops burden; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation with reserved GPU pools; Private gives full network isolation and customer control but adds ops and longer lead time.
[00:02:45] Jill Aaron: Curious on numbers - for our 200 rps bursts what does Dedicated look like capacity-wise vs Hosted?
[00:02:52] Maya Singh: For your payload sizes and aiming p95 200-300ms, Dedicated with a small pool (equivalent to 8-12 A100s depending on quantization) would handle large sustained periods and give headroom for burst. Hosted could handle bursts but you'd pay for egress and per-token at higher unit cost, and variability during noisy neighbors unless we provision fallback capacity. We'll make a sizing calc in the benchmark.
[00:03:18] Marcus Lee: Do you have example TCO numbers or a model? We need rough cost per 1M tokens and per-hour GPU cost to compare against our internal infra.
[00:03:26] Ethan Porter: Yes - we'll send a Dedicated pricing sheet and a comparative TCO model. Quick rule of thumb: Dedicated lowers per-token cost maybe 30-50% vs Hosted for consistent volume, but requires commitment. Private is similar to Dedicated plus onboarding and infra fees. Exact numbers depend on model choice and quantization.
[00:03:43] Sofia Ramos: On encryption - we need KMS integration and customer-managed keys; can Redwood support HSM-backed keys?
[00:03:50] Maya Singh: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated, and for Hosted we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with certain entitlements. We'll include details in the security doc.
[00:04:02] Danny Vu: On the models, are we locked to a single model or can we route to cheaper variants during load?
[00:04:07] Maya Singh: You can pin versions and set smart routing/fallback policies - e.g., route to a quantized variant during heavy load, or fall back to a lower-capacity region. That's part of the runtime. We'll demo that in benchmarks.
[00:04:24] Jill Aaron: What's the expected timeline for a POC that includes benchmarks and a short pilot?
[00:04:30] Ethan Porter: Typical path: week 0 - finalize success criteria and workload; week 1 - baseline profiling and infra prep; weeks 2-3 - 2-week benchmark window with hosted and dedicated configs; week 5 - evaluate results and propose pilot; pilot duration 6-12 weeks depending on scope. So roughly 6-10 weeks to get to a pilot decision.
[00:04:51] Marcus Lee: Ok that's reasonable. Regarding success criteria: we'll define latency p95 target (initially <300ms), throughput >=200 rps burst handling for at least 5 minutes, F1 >= current baseline, and cost target (example: cost per 1k requests < $X). We'll share exact numbers.
[00:05:10] Sofia Ramos: We need audit logs and per-request tracing for compliance reviews. Also RBAC and SSO integration - SAML or OIDC.
[00:05:18] Maya Singh: Those are standard - we have audit logging, tracing hooks, and SSO support. For Private we can integrate SAML with your IdP; for Dedicated we have similar controls. We'll include how logs are retained and redacted in the doc.
[00:05:30] Ethan Porter: A few common gotchas: KV cache warmup can skew latency initially, and quantized models save cost but sometimes change output slightly - we'll include evals to detect regressions. Also workload sampling matters: please give us samples representative of the token length and content.
[00:05:46] Danny Vu: For quality regressions what tooling do you provide? We run unit prompt sets with expected outputs.
[00:05:51] Maya Singh: We have an eval harness and can run regressions against your prompt set; produce a report with diffed outputs and aggregate metrics. We'll run that as part of the benchmark.
[00:06:05] Jill Aaron: If we go Private (on-prem), what's the onboarding timeline and who's responsible for infra?
[00:06:11] Ethan Porter: Private is the longest: typical onboarding 6-10 weeks plus your infra provisioning. Redwood's private control plane can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. We provide deployment docs, an installation window, and SE support during roll-out. Dedicated is faster - we can provision pools in 1-2 weeks after contract and network setup. Hosted is immediate.
[00:06:28] Marcus Lee: We also need to validate throughput at our region and with our dataset - can we run a dedicated benchmark in our region?
[00:06:34] Maya Singh: Yes we can run region-specific benchmarks; for Dedicated we can provision capacity in your preferred region as part of the POC if contract is agreed. For Hosted we'll run tests in the nearest Redwood region to your infra.
[00:06:47] Sofia Ramos: Any compliance exceptions for keeping PHI in Hosted?
[00:06:50] Ethan Porter: Hosted can be contractual but some customers prefer Dedicated/Private to meet strict PHI policies. We'll outline options and controls.
[00:06:59] Marcus Lee: On monitoring, can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?
[00:07:03] Maya Singh: Yes - Redwood Console exposes per-route, per-model dashboards, cost and latency breakdowns, and you'll get logs/traces. We'll provide sample screenshots in the deck.
[00:07:17] Jill Aaron: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[00:07:20] Ethan Porter: Recap: Redwood sends Dedicated pricing + TCO model, Maya sends security docs and VPC checklist, Horizon Health to share workload sample and exact success criteria. Aim to start benchmark window week of 2026-03-15. Any blockers?
[00:07:35] Sofia Ramos: None now, just need the SOC2 snapshot and KMS details.
[00:07:39] Marcus Lee: I'll prepare sample dataset and baseline metrics.
[00:07:44] Danny Vu: I'll coordinate the test harness and ensure secrets vetting.
[00:07:48] Ethan Porter: Great. We'll follow up via email and I'll put the benchmark plan in the spreadsheet. Thanks all.
[00:07:55] Jill Aaron: Thanks everyone.
[00:08:00] [call ends]

Notes about transcript quality: Some transcription artifacts present - product names like "k-v cache" sometimes transcribed as "kayv cache"; a few overlaps and filler words remain. Shared artifacts: deck link (to be shared), security doc (SOC2 snapshot), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).

POC Acceptance Criteria (as captured on call):
- Latency: p95 < 300ms (goal < 200ms)
- Throughput: handle 200 rps bursts for 5+ min without failure, sustained 40-60 rps
- Quality: no regression on key entity F1 compared to baseline
- Security: KMS/BYOK support, audit logs, RBAC/SSO, data residency in region (US-EAST preferred)
- Timeline: benchmark window starting week of 2026-03-15, evaluation by end of March, pilot decision by mid-April

References mentioned:
- Redwood Dedicated pricing deck (will be shared)
- SOC2 snapshot and security docs (Maya to share)
- Benchmark spreadsheet (Ethan to share)

End of transcript.
